title: 6 best OB-GYN scheduling software picks for July 2026
summary: OB/GYN no-shows run 18 to 28%. See how 4 scheduling tools compare on EHR write-back, billing, after-hours support, and payer-facing call coverage.
body_markdown:
OB/GYN scheduling software is a category of patient access tools built to handle the specific call mix of an OB/GYN practice — prenatal scheduling, insurance questions, postpartum follow-ups, and after-hours calls — that general-purpose scheduling tools often only cover half of. That gap matters more in OB/GYN than in most specialties:[no-show rates average 18%](https://www.solutionreach.com/blog/which-wins-the-national-average-no-show-rate-or-yours-1) and[climb to 28% for high-risk visits](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11074955/) , and a missed slot here can mean a delayed prenatal check or a lost IVF cycle window, not just a routine reschedule.


Most vendor pages compare features in isolation; this ranking scores each tool against the full OB/GYN call mix, from scheduling through insurance and after-hours coverage, so the comparison reflects what a practice actually experiences across a billing cycle, not just a demo. We ranked six tools against the criteria that actually matter for OB/GYN call volume and stakes.

- OB/GYN scheduling software handles the calendar plus the insurance, billing, and after-hours calls a general-purpose tool leaves to staff.
- No-shows average 18%, and unfilled slots often mean a missed prenatal visit, high-risk monitoring appointment, or IVF cycle window, not just a routine follow-up, and each one is a visit that never gets billed.

- Prosper AI resolves over 60% of inbound calls end-to-end in production, covering scheduling, benefits verification, and after-hours volume, keeping more visits financially cleared before the patient ever reaches the front desk (based on Prosper AI's customer deployment data).


## What is OB/GYN Scheduling Software?


Scheduling software built for OB/GYN practices handles the appointment workflows that general-purpose tools often miss, like booking prenatal visits across trimesters, managing recurring postpartum checkups, and routing new patients to the right provider based on gestational age or insurance. Understanding[AI patient scheduling](https://getprosper.ai/blog/ai-patient-scheduling-guide) helps clarify what to look for when vetting these tools.


At its core, OB/GYN scheduling software connects patient intake, calendar management, and EHR data so front desk staff spend less time on coordination and more time on exceptions that genuinely need a human.


## Why OB/GYN Scheduling Gaps Cost More Than in Other Specialties


[OB/GYN no-show rates average 18%](https://www.solutionreach.com/blog/which-wins-the-national-average-no-show-rate-or-yours-1) and climb to 28% for high-risk and specialty subsets. One 151,435-appointment health system audit found[26.5% of scheduled visits went unfilled](https://dexcare.com/resources/articles/patient-no-show-rates/) , costing over 10,000 provider hours a year.[New-patient wait times now average 42 days](https://ir.amnhealthcare.com/2025-05-27-New-Survey-Shows-Physician-Appointment-Wait-Times-Surge-19-Since-2022,-48-Since-2004) , up 79% since 2004 — the largest increase of any specialty tracked.


## How We Ranked OB/GYN Scheduling Software


OB/GYN practices handle calls that stretch well beyond calendar management. Prenatal care cadence appointments, sensitive reproductive health inquiries, and insurance verification tied to gestational age raise the administrative stakes considerably. A scheduling tool that covers half the call types may look adequate in a demo and fall short by month two.


We ranked tools against eight criteria:


- EHR and PMS integration depth (read and write, not read-only)
- Call resolution breadth beyond scheduling: billing, insurance, refills, and FAQs
- AI architecture generation: scripted workflows vs. goal-driven agents
- After-hours and weekend coverage
- Inbound and outbound automation
- [HIPAA compliance](https://www.oncehub.com/blog/hipaa-compliant-scheduling-software)
- Multilingual support
- Time to go live


Narrow-scope tools carry above-average front-desk risk in OB/GYN. When a practice's call mix includes insurance plan restrictions, gestational routing rules, and sensitive inquiry types, a tool that only handles scheduling leaves a large share of daily volume unresolved.

### 2. Artera


Artera is a patient communication tool built around messaging, appointment reminders, and two-way texting across SMS, email, and web chat.


**What it offers:**


- Two-way texting so patients confirm, cancel, or reschedule directly from a reminder message without calling the front desk
- Integration with many major EHRs, used across a wide range of specialties
- Reminder automation that can meaningfully reduce inbound confirmation calls for high-volume OB/GYN practices


**Good for** : Practices whose main need is reducing confirmation calls through messaging and reminders.


**Limitation** : Focuses on messaging workflows only. Does not handle inbound phone calls, prior auth, or benefits verification, so front desk staff still own those call types manually.


**Bottom line** : See a full[Prosper AI vs Artera](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/prosper-ai-vs-artera-which-is-better-for-your-practice) comparison for a deeper breakdown.


### 3. Assort Health


Assort Health is an AI-powered scheduling tool built for high-volume specialty practices, focused on patient self-scheduling and slot optimization.


**What it offers:**


- Online portal for patients to book appointments without calling the front desk
- Integration with several major EHR systems
- Provider matching based on insurance, visit type, and availability


**Good for** : Practices looking to reduce scheduling errors and front-desk call volume through self-scheduling.


**Limitation** : Largely a scheduling point solution. Handles the calendar well but leaves prior auth, benefits verification, and after-hours call handling to staff.


**Bottom line** : A solid fit if self-scheduling and slot optimization are the only front-desk pain points. See a full[Prosper AI vs Assort Health](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/prosper-ai-assort-health-review) comparison for a deeper breakdown.


### 4. Hello Patient


Hello Patient is a patient communication and scheduling tool built for specialty practices. Its AI agent, Mia, handles inbound calls, text, and chat around the clock, covering scheduling, rescheduling, and routine patient questions.


**What it offers:**


- Two-way text messaging so patients confirm, cancel, or reschedule directly from an appointment reminder without calling the office
- Self-scheduling portal for patients to book available slots based on provider-configured rules
- A straightforward interface that keeps staff training time low


**Good for** : Practices whose main need is reminders and self-scheduling, not full inbound/outbound call handling.


**Limitation** : Hello Patient's AI agent handles patient-facing billing conversations — explaining balances and facilitating payment — but does not perform payer-side RCM work such as claims submission, denials management, or outbound payor calling.


**Bottom line** : Practices with high call volume often find they need additional tools to cover what Hello Patient leaves unhandled. See a full[Prosper AI vs Hello Patient](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/prosper-ai-vs-hello-patient-review) comparison for a deeper breakdown.


### 5. EliseAI


Founded in 2017 in property management, EliseAI entered healthcare in 2023. Its architecture pairs an LLM for speech generation with a workflow engine that enforces linear call flows instead of goal-driven conversation management.


**What it offers:**


- Voice and text automation for scheduling and administrative inquiries
- Inbound scheduling suited to practices with stable, predictable visit patterns
- Capability quality that varies by deployment configuration


**Good for** : Practices with low-variance scheduling workflows and no requirement for RCM or payer-facing call handling.


**Limitation** : Linear call flows can break down on mid-call topic pivots, off-script insurance questions, and the complex multi-turn conversations common in prenatal and high-risk OB calls. Scripted-workflow tools generally reach an all-inbound resolution ceiling of roughly 25-40%.


**Bottom line:** Adequate for predictable scheduling patterns, but architecture and deployment variance tend to leave gaps for practices with high call complexity or RCM requirements. See a full[Prosper AI vs EliseAI](https://www.getprosper.ai/blog/prosper-ai-vs-eliseai) comparison for a deeper breakdown.


### 6. Luma Health


Luma Health markets its voice AI product as "Spark." In practice, it's an SMS and text workflow tool with voice AI that has limited documented production deployment.


**What it offers:**


- SMS and text automation for patient reminders, confirmations, and cancellations
- SMS-to-form deflection for a subset of scheduling inquiriesVoice AI with limited published production case studies, focused on cancellations
- Text-based patient communication campaigns


**Good for** : Practices whose primary need is reducing no-shows through SMS reminders for simple appointment types.


**Limitation** : SMS-first tools typically lack EHR write-back and outbound voice. SMS deflection rates in the 15-25% range are not the same as end-to-end call resolution.


**Bottom line** : A workable starting point for SMS-based no-show reduction, but OB/GYN practices needing end-to-end scheduling, insurance, and billing handling will find it falls short. ## Frequently Asked Questions


**How do I choose between Prosper AI, EliseAI, and Assort Health for my OB/GYN practice?**


Start by mapping your actual call mix across three months of data. If your volume is limited to predictable appointment scheduling, Assort Health or EliseAI may be adequate. If your front desk also handles insurance verification, billing inquiries, referral status, and after-hours calls, Prosper AI is the only option on this list with documented production coverage across that full range, resolving over 60% of inbound calls end-to-end based on Prosper AI's customer deployment data.


**What should I test before selecting any OB/GYN scheduling software?**


Call a live customer number for each vendor you are vetting and test three things: whether the agent can answer questions it was not scripted for, whether it can follow a caller who changes topics mid-call, and whether it handles a mid-call language switch. These tests take 10 to 15 minutes per vendor and expose capability gaps that demos typically do not show.


**Is Prosper AI a good fit for smaller OB/GYN practices or independent clinics?**


Prosper AI is built for outpatient groups with 5+ locations. Independent single-site practices may find the product's scope exceeds their current call volume, and tools like Hello Patient or Artera may offer a lower-friction entry point for reminder and messaging workflows. Practices with 5+ locations and high mixed call volume are a stronger fit.


**How much do OB/GYN no-shows cost in lost revenue and provider time?**


[No-show rates in OB/GYN average around 18%](https://www.solutionreach.com/blog/which-wins-the-national-average-no-show-rate-or-yours-1) . One 12-month audit of a health system's OB/GYN department, covering 151,435 scheduled appointments, found[26.5% went unfilled by no-shows or cancellations that were never backfilled](https://dexcare.com/resources/articles/patient-no-show-rates/) , costing over 10,000 provider hours a year. The dollar cost varies by practice size and payer mix, but the hours lost to unfilled slots are a fixed, recurring cost regardless of specialty pricing.


**Why are OB/GYN wait times increasing, and can scheduling software help?**


N[ew-patient OB/GYN wait times now average 42 days](https://ir.amnhealthcare.com/2025-05-27-New-Survey-Shows-Physician-Appointment-Wait-Times-Surge-19-Since-2022,-48-Since-2004) , up 33% since 2022 and 79% since 2004, the largest percentage increase of any specialty tracked. The main driver isn't scheduling inefficiency. It's a genuine physician shortage ([roughly 93.4% of demand currently met](https://medicushcs.com/resources/insights-into-the-growing-obgyn-shortage) , and worsening) combined with hospital OB-unit closures reducing available capacity. Scheduling software can't fix a supply problem. What it can do is absorb the rising call volume that comes with it: filling cancelled slots faster, reducing the no-shows that make wait times worse, and freeing staff to handle the exceptions that actually need a human.
